description: Short paraphrased summaries written for testing retrieval. They are NOT regulatory text and must not be loaded as a source; the real corpus is ingested from the official sources in Phase 11.3.

corpus.title: Reports by brokers or dealers in securities of suspicious transactions
corpus.text:
A broker-dealer must file a suspicious activity report (SAR) for a transaction conducted through it that involves funds or assets of at least $5,000 when it knows, suspects or has reason to suspect the transaction involves illegal activity, is designed to evade reporting requirements, has no business or apparent lawful purpose, or uses the broker-dealer to facilitate criminal activity.

The SAR must be filed no later than 30 calendar days after the date of initial detection of the facts that form the basis for filing. If no suspect is identified, filing may be delayed a further 30 calendar days. Supporting documentation must be retained for five years. The filing is confidential and the subject must not be notified.

corpus.title: Customer identification programs for broker-dealers
corpus.text:
A broker-dealer must maintain a written customer identification program (CIP). Before opening an account it must obtain, at a minimum, the customer's name, date of birth for an individual, address and an identification number such as a taxpayer identification number or passport number.

The program must include risk-based procedures to verify the identity of each customer within a reasonable time, through documents or non-documentary methods, keep records of the information obtained, and check whether the customer appears on designated government lists.

corpus.title: Beneficial ownership requirements for legal entity customers
corpus.text: Covered financial institutions must identify and verify the beneficial owners of legal entity customers when a new account is opened. Beneficial owners are each individual who owns, directly or indirectly, 25 percent or more of the equity interests of the legal entity, and one individual with significant responsibility to control or manage the entity, such as a chief executive officer or managing member.

corpus.title: Filing obligations for reports of transactions in currency
corpus.text: A financial institution must file a currency transaction report (CTR) for each deposit, withdrawal, exchange of currency or other payment or transfer by, through or to the institution that involves a transaction in currency of more than $10,000. Multiple currency transactions are treated as one if the institution knows they are by or on behalf of the same person and total more than $10,000 in a single business day.

corpus.title: Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Program
corpus.text: Each member firm must develop and implement a written anti-money laundering program approved in writing by senior management. The program must establish policies and internal controls to detect and report suspicious transactions, provide for independent testing of the program, designate an AML compliance person responsible for day-to-day operation, and provide ongoing training for appropriate personnel.

corpus.title: Periodic KYC review cycles
corpus.text: High-risk customers are re-reviewed every 12 months, medium-risk customers every 24 months and low-risk customers every 36 months. A review is also triggered by a material change in ownership, a sanctions or PEP screening hit, or an escalated alert. Reviews that are overdue by more than 30 days are reported to the MLRO.
